cross_verification.note_en: Every attempted WebFetch of Peru's unified government portal (gob.pe, which hosts Superintendencia Nacional de Migraciones' passport pages) returned HTTP 418 ('I'm a Teapot'), a deliberate anti-bot response, on both the specific passport-service page and the bare domain root. migraciones.gob.pe redirects (301) to the same blocked gob.pe domain. consulado.pe (Peru's consular site, which hosts a visa-application PDF referencing passport-photo standards) returned a certificate-validation error on every attempt. As a result no composition field could be independently confirmed from a Peruvian government source in this research pass; the official_source_url above is included only because it was confirmed to be the correct authority's page via multiple independent search-result listings (titled/branded as the Superintendencia Nacional de Migraciones' own 'Plataforma del Estado Peruano' page), not because its content was read. Note for a human reviewer: secondary Peruvian press reporting (not used as a source here, since it is not a government domain) suggests the passport photo in Peru is captured biometrically on-site at the Migraciones office at the time of the appointment rather than submitted by the applicant, which — if accurate — would make a fixed print-photo size/background spec largely inapplicable to this document type; this should be confirmed directly against gob.pe before publishing.
